title: The booking service core
idea: The core modules are the entities, the repositories that store them, and `BookingService`, which runs each use case by combining them through constructor injection.
points: Repositories hide storage and reach `BookingService` through its constructor.
`searchFree` keeps rooms that are big enough, then drops any room that clashes.
`book` asks the policy first and saves only when the slot is free.
`cancel` finds the booking and refuses anyone who is not its owner.

steps.caption: Employee E7 asks for room `R-101` from 10 to 11.
`BookingService` builds a candidate `Booking` and loads the room's bookings with `forRoom`.
`ConflictPolicy` finds no overlap, so the candidate may go ahead.
`BookingRepository` saves it. Only now does the id counter move on.
The saved `Booking` returns to the caller.
A second request asks for the same room from 10:30 to 12:00.
This time `ConflictPolicy` finds an overlap with the first booking.
The service throws before saving, so the repository never sees the clash.

code.title: Service and repositories
code.caption: The core in one file: search, book, cancel, repository interfaces with in-memory versions, and an injected policy.

walk.text: Dependencies arrive through the constructor as interfaces and stay `private final`.
Search keeps rooms big enough, then drops rooms that `clash`, the helper `book` also uses.
Book checks first, then takes the id and saves; a refusal changes nothing.
Cancel finds the booking, refuses anyone but its owner, then removes it.
Repositories are interfaces; `main` picks in-memory ones, so a database version needs no service change.
`main` wires the parts by hand; the overlap rule is a lambda.
Refusals are an `IllegalStateException` for now; the next page gives errors their own types.

pitfalls: Do not let `BookingService` create its repositories; inject them so tests can swap them.
Never save before checking conflicts; a refused booking must leave storage unchanged.
Do not advance the id counter before the check passes, or refusals waste ids.

quiz.q: After `BK1` (R-101, 10 to 11) is saved, what does this print?
quiz.code:
// R-101 seats 6, R-201 seats 12, R-301 seats 4
System.out.println("free: " + svc.searchFree(5, 11, 12));
quiz.why: `R-301` seats only 4. `BK1` ends at 11, and `11 < 11` is false, so a back-to-back slot does not clash.

takeaway: Inject the parts, check before you save, keep storage behind a repository.
